title: Product-first strategy and expert-reasoning separation
research_question: How should the project organize product capability, expert procedural knowledge, empirical calibration and paper production without allowing manuscript needs to distort the system?
before_state: The work could have remained manuscript-led, while declarative rules, expert inference procedure, response behavior and empirical calibration risked being treated as one undifferentiated object.
result: The accepted project rationale prioritizes a reliable, traceable product and separates canonical declarative knowledge (Kc), response knowledge (Kr), inference policy (π), empirical calibration parameters (θ) and individual state belief (b). Manuscript prose is treated as an output/snapshot rather than the project's memory.
key_insights: The product should earn academic claims through its actual formalization, validation and later empirical evidence.
Knowing what a source rule says differs from knowing how an expert orders and combines rules.
Textbook expert cases support method-fidelity reconstruction; they are not automatically real-world probability labels.
Different accuracy questions must remain separate: chart calculation, source-rule fidelity, inference consistency, blind prediction and calibration/abstention.
negative_findings: A single aggregate accuracy number is not sufficient to characterize the system.

boundaries.source_status: Accepted project architecture and historical rationale, not a classical-source claim.
boundaries.implementation_status: Product architecture and roadmap specify the separation; individual runtime components have their own maturity states.
boundaries.internal_fidelity: Must be assessed through the relevant benchmark, not inferred from architecture existence.
boundaries.empirical_status: No predictive increment is claimed by this design event.

authority_notes: This is an accepted project-method rationale. It does not mean all Product v0.4 components or empirical calibration are complete.
